subject.title: fix(gateway): regenerate native hook descriptors when relay unavailable after restart

question: When the Codex app-server native relay cannot be invoked, should OpenClaw fall back to generic before_tool_call policy evaluation or remain fail-closed until relay re-registration succeeds?
rationale: Both paths can enforce policy in principle, but repository history deliberately protects unknown unavailable states and the PR has no live proof that the generic path is equivalent across trusted policy, plugin approvals, and user prompts.

options.title: Prove guarded fallback
options.body: Accept fallback only after exact-head live restart or drain evidence shows native tools recover and all enforcement and approval layers still execute.

options.title: Require relay recovery
options.body: Keep app-server relay failures blocked and repair or refresh relay registration before allowing native tools to continue.

options.title: Accept fallback contract
options.body: Explicitly make generic policy fallback permanent for relay invocation failures and document the security-boundary choice.

recommendation.title: Prove guarded fallback
recommendation.body: Accept fallback only after exact-head live restart or drain evidence shows native tools recover and all enforcement and approval layers still execute.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-history signal is the guarded fallback contract they authored and merged across these relay paths.
